companyDescription: AI accelerator GPU + CPU powerhouse · MI400 HBM4 GPU H2 2026 · AMD Advancing AI event Jul 22-23 in SF · Meta 6GW Instinct deal + EPYC Venice hyperscaler ramp
priceNote: Fell 6.97% Jul 7 on a Reuters report that China's DeepSeek is developing its own AI inference chip — a sector-wide semiconductor selloff (PHLX -4.65%), not an AMD-specific setback. Comes one day after Goldman Sachs raised its PT to $640 from $450.
summary: AMD dropped nearly 7% on Jul 7 as a broad AI-chip selloff — triggered by a Reuters report that DeepSeek is building its own proprietary inference chip — outweighed a fresh Goldman Sachs price-target raise to $640 (from $450, Jul 5) on the agentic AI CPU thesis. Meta has committed to deploying up to 6GW of AMD Instinct GPUs and is a lead customer for 6th-gen EPYC Venice CPUs; AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Tencent have all expanded EPYC-powered instances. AMD Advancing AI 2026 (Jul 22-23, San Francisco) — the MI400/Helios full reveal — is now 14 days out, with Q2 earnings following on Aug 4.

catalysts.name: AMD Advancing AI 2026 — July 22-23 SF
catalysts.description: AMD's flagship annual AI conference at Moscone Center. Lisa Su leads. MI400 full technical reveal (432GB HBM4), Helios rack-scale platform, ROCm roadmap, and hyperscaler deployment timeline — AMD's GTC moment, now more important given the post-selloff reset.

catalysts.name: DeepSeek Proprietary AI Chip Report
catalysts.description: Jul 7, 2026: Reuters reported China's DeepSeek is designing its own AI inference chip, potentially reducing dependence on third-party suppliers like AMD/NVIDIA. Triggered a sector-wide selloff; still early-stage and unconfirmed as a shipping product.

catalysts.name: MI400 Production Shipments H2 2026
catalysts.description: 432GB HBM4 memory per GPU, Helios rack with 72x MI455X accelerators. Production shipments expected mid-2026; Microsoft, Meta and other hyperscalers are key early adopters.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Expected Aug 4, 2026. Market watches for AI GPU/data-center revenue continuation and MI350 ramp, plus any commentary responding to the DeepSeek chip headlines.

risks: DeepSeek reportedly developing a proprietary AI inference chip (Reuters, Jul 7) — a long-term competitive risk to third-party suppliers like AMD if it ships and gains traction, though development timelines for AI silicon are long and uncertain

Sector-wide de-rating risk: PHLX Semiconductor Index -4.65% same day, Micron -22% off its ATH — AMD's move looks more macro/sector-driven than company-specific, but that also means it can keep falling with the group
ROCm software ecosystem still 2-3 years behind NVIDIA's CUDA — limits AMD's AI training market-share ceiling
MI400 execution risk — any production delay announced at the Advancing AI event would be a sharp reversal catalyst
Consensus median PT ~$485 (29 analysts, 6-month trailing) is still below the post-selloff price — the newest bullish targets (Goldman $640, Cantor $700) haven't been matched by the broader Street yet
FOMC Jul 29 lands one week after the Advancing AI event — a second event-risk window

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75%; next FOMC Jul 28-29, one week after the Advancing AI event. June CPI (Jul 14) is the next inflation checkpoint.
macroRisk.inflationNote: No cuts priced for 2026. AMD's data-center products are enterprise capex — somewhat rate-sensitive, but locked-in hyperscaler AI budgets (Meta's 6GW commitment) provide a demand floor.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: HIGH near-term impact from the Jul 7 sector-wide de-rating (semis led the tech selloff on DeepSeek + AI-valuation worries), but the Advancing AI event (Jul 22) is a company-specific catalyst independent of the macro calendar.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk MEDIUM — the immediate driver of the Jul 7 drop was sector sentiment (DeepSeek headlines, AI-valuation worries), not Fed policy. Advancing AI Jul 22 is the near-term re-rate trigger; FOMC Jul 29 is the risk to manage after it.

entryStrategy.verdict: Buy the post-DeepSeek-headline dip pre-event — scale in near the 50-day MA ($470-485) for best R/R. Target $615-700 by Q3. Trim on strength around Advancing AI (Jul 22-23); hold remainder into Q2 earnings Aug 4.

catalystSpot.preRunup: AMD historically runs 8-15% in the 2-3 weeks before its major AI events. Ahead of Advancing AI 2025, the stock ran +12% over 3 weeks as buy-the-event positioning built. The current post-DeepSeek-headline pullback resets that setup at a lower starting price.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 2-3 สัปดาห์ก่อน event (ตั้งแต่ตอนนี้ถึง 22 ก.ค.)

postWin.note: AMD Advancing AI 2025: MI300X full reveal + Lisa Su roadmap — stock +28% over 2 weeks. AMD's GTC-equivalent events historically show 10-25% post-event moves when the product exceeds expectations.

postLose.note: AMD Q3 2024 earnings (Oct 2024): MI300X ramp slower than expected — stock -12% in 2 days. A DeepSeek chip confirmation or MI400 delay announcement would risk a similar move.

spotSizing.reason: Event-driven play with a clear 14-day catalyst. 6% sizing given the fresh ~7% pullback creates a better entry, but the DeepSeek headline is a real (if early-stage) long-term risk worth respecting — scale to 8-10% only after the event confirms the roadmap.

comparableCases.event: AMD Advancing AI 2025 — MI300X Full Reveal
comparableCases.note: Lisa Su unveiled MI300X full specs at Advancing AI 2025 — stock +28% over 2 weeks as hyperscaler adoption was confirmed. Advancing AI 2026 with MI400 is the identical setup.

NVIDIA's GTC Blackwell reveal drove the stock +20% in 1 week. AMD's Advancing AI is its equivalent event; MI400 with 432GB HBM4 is a significant leap that could generate similar excitement if delivered as promised.
